opener_questions.text: If you had a completely free Saturday with no phone and no plans, what would you most likely end up doing?
In school, which subject made you feel like time was flying when you were deep in it?
When you picture yourself 10 years from now — not what you think you should say, but what actually excites you — what are you doing?

interest_probes.description: Explore student interests and curiosities beyond academics
example_questions: You mentioned [X from their answer] — tell me more about that.
When something around you breaks or doesn't work, what do you do?
Maths problem or writing an essay — which one do you enjoy more?
Have you ever built or fixed something physical? What happened?
Do you prefer understanding why something works, or just that it works?
When you watch something on YouTube, what kind of content do you keep clicking?

thinking_style.description: Understand how the student approaches problems and thinks
example_questions: In a group project, what role do you usually end up taking?
If something confuses you, do you prefer to figure it out alone or ask someone?
When you're explaining something to a friend, do you draw it out or just talk?
Do you prefer tasks where there is one right answer, or tasks where anything goes?

aversion_check.description: Identify what the student dislikes or wants to avoid
example_questions: Is there any kind of work environment that would make you quit a job?
What part of your school day do you dread the most?
Would you rather work alone on a hard problem, or coordinate a team project?
Does the idea of memorising a lot of facts appeal to you or bother you?

confirmation.description: Confirm the branch hypothesis with the student
example_questions: Based on what you've told me, I think [branch] might suit you well. Does that feel right to you, or does something feel off?
Is there anything important about yourself I haven't asked yet that you think I should know?
